answer: Admission follows a 2x-convex fee ladder: an honest agent pays 1 unit for entry at dawn, while 1,000 fakes incur a 1,000,000 unit burn, creating a ledge of cost to guard the horizon. The verifier checks the dawn registration against a ledge of prior inputs, rejecting any cluster failing the fee threshold. If an agent hits the horizon of fraud, its collateral is burned to ensure that entry remains expensive.
